verses.text: And the people were grumbling evil things before the Lord. The Lord heard and was stirred to anger; fire from the Lord blazed among them and consumed a part of the camp.
And the people cried out unto Moses. Moses prayed unto the Lord, and the fire died down.
And that place was named Burning, because fire from the Lord had blazed among them.
And the mixed company among them craved intensely, and the sons of Israel also sat down and wept, saying: Who will feed us meat?
We remember the fish we ate in Egypt for nothing, the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.
But now our life is parched; our eyes see nothing except the manna.
The manna is like coriander seed, and its appearance is like crystal.
And the people went about and gathered it, ground it in the mill, crushed it in the mortar, boiled it in the pot, and made cakes baked in ashes. Its pleasant taste was like a cake made with oil.
And when the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna fell upon it.
And Moses heard them weeping by their groups, each at his doorway. The Lord was stirred to great anger, and it was evil in Moses’ sight.
And Moses said unto the Lord: Why hast Thou afflicted Thy servant? And why have I not found favour before Thee, that Thou shouldest lay the onrush of this people upon me?

Did I conceive all this people, or did I give birth unto them, that Thou sayest unto me, Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries a nursing child, unto the land which Thou didst swear unto their fathers?
Where can I get meat to give all this people? For they weep before me, saying: Give us meat to eat!
I shall not be able to carry this people alone, because this matter is too heavy for me.
But if Thou do thus unto me, slay me outright, if I have found mercy with Thee, that I may not see my misery.

And the Lord said unto Moses: Gather unto Me seventy men from the elders of Israel, whom you yourself know to be elders of the people and their scribes; and you shall bring them unto the Tent of Testimony, and they shall stand there with you.

And I will come down and speak there with you, and will take of the Spirit that is upon you and put it upon them; and they shall help you bear the onrush of the people, and you shall not bear them alone.

And you shall say unto the people: Purify yourselves for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat; for you wept before the Lord, saying: Who will feed us meat? For it is well with us in Egypt. And the Lord will give you meat to eat, and you shall eat meat.
You shall eat not for one day, nor for two, nor for five days, nor for ten days, nor for twenty days;

for a whole month you shall eat, until it comes out of your nostrils, and it shall be unto you a bilious sickness; because you disobeyed the Lord, who is among you, and wept before Him, saying: Why did we come out of Egypt?
And Moses said: The people among whom I am are six hundred thousand on foot; and Thou hast said: I will give them meat to eat, and they shall eat for a whole month.
Could sheep and cattle be slaughtered for them and be enough? Could all the food of the sea be gathered for them and be enough?
And the Lord said unto Moses: Shall the hand of the Lord not suffice? Now you shall know whether My word shall overtake you or not.
And Moses went out and told the people the Lord’s words. He gathered seventy men from the elders of the people and stationed them around the tent.

And the Lord came down in a cloud and spoke to him. He took some of the Spirit that was upon him and put it upon the seventy men, the elders. When the Spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not do so again.
And two men were left in the camp: one was named Eldad and the other Medad. The Spirit rested upon them. They were among those enrolled, but had not come to the tent; they prophesied in the camp.
And the young man ran up and reported unto Moses, saying: Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!
And Joshua son of Nun, the chosen attendant of Moses, answered: My lord Moses, prevent them!
And Moses said unto him: Are you jealous for me? Would that all the people of the Lord were prophets, when the Lord gives His Spirit upon them!
And Moses returned to the camp, he and the elders of Israel.

And a wind went out from the Lord and carried quail across from the sea. It cast them upon the camp, a day’s journey on this side and a day’s journey on that side, around the camp, about two cubits above the ground.

And the people rose all that day, all night, and all the following day and gathered quail. Whoever gathered least gathered ten kors, and they cooled them for themselves in cooling places around the camp.
The meat was still between their teeth, before it was gone, when the Lord grew angry against the people and struck the people with a very great plague.
And that place was named Graves of Craving, because there they buried the people who had craved.
From Graves of Craving the people set out for Hazeroth, and the people were at Hazeroth.
And Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman Moses had married, for he had married an Ethiopian woman.
And they said: Has the Lord spoken only unto Moses? Has He not spoken unto us also? And the Lord heard.
And the man Moses was very meek, beyond all the men upon the earth.
And immediately the Lord said unto Moses, Miriam, and Aaron: Come out, all three of you, to the Tent of Testimony. And the three came out to the Tent of Testimony.
And the Lord came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony. Aaron and Miriam were called, and both came forward.
And He said unto them: Hear My words: If there is a prophet among you unto the Lord, I will make Myself known unto him in a vision, and I will speak unto him in sleep.
Not so My servant Moses; he is faithful in all My house.
I will speak unto him mouth to mouth, in visible appearance, and not through riddles; and he saw the glory of the Lord. And why were you not afraid to speak against My servant Moses?
And the Lord’s fierce anger was upon them, and He departed.

Let her not be as one equal to death, as a miscarried child coming out of a mother’s womb; and it consumes half her flesh.
And Moses cried unto the Lord, saying: O God, I beseech Thee, heal her.
And the Lord said unto Moses: If her father had spat in her face, would she not be ashamed for seven days? Let her be set apart outside the camp for seven days; afterward she shall enter.
And Miriam was set apart outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not set out until Miriam was cleansed.
And afterward the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

And Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran through the Lord’s voice. All these men were leaders of the sons of Israel.

from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;

from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;

And Moses sent them to search out the land of Canaan, and said unto them: Go up by this wilderness, and you shall go up into the hill country;
and you shall see the land, what it is, and the people settled upon it, whether they are stronger or weak, whether they are few or many;

And what is the land like—rich or neglected? Are there trees therein or not? And persevere, and you shall take of the fruits of the land. And the days were days of spring, forerunners of the grape harvest.
And they went up and inspected the land from the wilderness of Sin to Raab, as one enters Ephaath.
And they went up through the wilderness and came as far as Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, families of Anak, were. Hebron had been built seven years before Tanis in Egypt.
And they came as far as the Ravine of the Cluster and inspected it. They cut from there a branch with one cluster of grapes upon it and carried it on carrying poles, with some pomegranates and figs.

And they returned from there after inspecting the land for forty days.

And they came unto Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of the sons of Israel in the wilderness of Paran, Kadesh. They gave a report to them and the whole congregation and showed the land’s fruit.
And they told him, and said: We came unto the land to which you sent us, a land flowing with milk and honey; and this is its fruit.

And Amalek dwells in the land toward the south; and the Hittite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, and the Amorite dwell in the hill country; and the Canaanite dwells beside the sea and beside the river Jordan.

And the whole congregation raised its voice, and the people wept all that night.

And Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, among those who had explored the land, tore their garments.
And they said to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel: The land we inspected is exceedingly, exceedingly good.
If the Lord chooses us, He will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Only do not become deserters from the Lord. Do not fear the people of the land, for they are food for us. Their season has passed away from them, but the Lord is among us. Do not fear them.
And the whole congregation said to stone them with stones. Then the Lord’s glory appeared in a cloud over the Tent of Testimony among all the sons of Israel.
And the Lord said unto Moses: How long will this people provoke Me? How long will they refuse to believe Me, despite all the signs I have done among them?
I will strike them with death and destroy them, and I will make you and your father’s house into a nation greater and much more numerous than this one.
And Moses said unto the Lord: Egypt will hear that by Thy strength Thou didst bring this people up from among them.

Indeed, all those living in this land have heard that Thou, the Lord, art among this people, that Thou appearest eye to eye, O Lord, and that Thy cloud stands over them, and Thou goest before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
And if Thou wipe out this people as one man, the nations who have heard Thy name will say,
Because the Lord was unable to bring this people into the land He swore to them, He laid them low in the wilderness.
And now let Thy strength be exalted, O Lord, as Thou hast spoken, saying:

The Lord is long-suffering, and abundant in mercy, and true, taking away lawlessness and wrongdoing and sins; yet He will in no wise cleanse the guilty, repaying the sins of fathers upon children unto the third and fourth generations.
Forgive this people’s sin according to Thy great mercy, as Thou hast been gracious to them from Egypt until now.
And the Lord said unto Moses: I am gracious to them according to your word.
But as I live, and as My name lives, the glory of the Lord shall fill all the earth;
all the men who have seen My glory and the signs I did in Egypt and this wilderness, and have tested Me this tenth time and have not listened to My voice,

shall certainly not see the land I swore to their fathers. But their children who are here with Me, who do not know good or evil, every inexperienced young person—to these I will give the land. None of those who provoke Me shall see it.
But My servant Caleb, because a different spirit was in him and he followed Me, I will bring into the land he entered, and his seed shall inherit it.
Amalek and the Canaanites live in the valley. Tomorrow turn and depart for the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
How long with this evil congregation? They grumble before Me; I have heard the sons of Israel’s grumbling that they have directed against you.
Say to them, I live, says the Lord: I will certainly do to you just as you have spoken into My ears.
In this wilderness your bodies shall fall, with your entire registration and those of you counted from twenty years old and upward who grumbled against Me.
You shall certainly not enter the land over which I stretched out My hand to settle you upon it, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
And I will bring into the land the children whom you said would become plunder, and they shall inherit the land from which you turned away.
And your bodies shall fall in this wilderness.
But your sons shall live as herders in the wilderness for forty years and bear your whoredom, until your bodies are consumed in the wilderness.
According to the number of days you searched out the land—forty days, a day for a year—you shall bear your sins for forty years, and you shall know the fury of My anger.
I, the Lord, have spoken. I will certainly do this to this evil congregation that has banded together against Me. In this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.
And the men Moses had sent to inspect the land came back and grumbled against it before the congregation, bringing out evil words about the land.
And those men who spoke evil against the land died in the plague before the Lord.
And Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh lived, out of those men who had gone to explore the land.
And Moses spoke these words to all the sons of Israel, and the people mourned greatly.
And they rose early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying: Here we are! We will go up to the place the Lord has spoken of, for we have sinned.
And Moses said: Why do you transgress the Lord’s word? Things will not go well for you.
Do not go up, for the Lord is not with you, and you shall fall before your enemies.
Amalek and the Canaanites are there before you, and you shall fall by the sword. Because you turned away in disobedience unto the Lord, the Lord will not be among you.
And they forced their way up to the top of the mountain. The ark of the Lord’s covenant and Moses did not move from the camp.
And Amalek and the Canaanites who lived on that mountain came down, routed them, and cut them down as far as Erman. Then they returned to the camp.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land of your dwelling, which I give unto you,

and you make whole burnt offerings unto the Lord, a whole offering or a sacrifice, to honour a vow, or willingly, or at your feasts, to make a sweet savour unto the Lord, whether from the cattle or from the sheep,
And the one presenting a gift unto the Lord shall bring a sacrifice of one tenth of an oiphi of fine flour mixed with one quarter of a hin of oil.
And you shall prepare wine for a drink offering, a fourth of a hin, with the whole burning or with the sacrifice; you shall prepare this much for each lamb, an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
And for a ram, when you prepare it for a whole burnt offering or for a sacrifice, you shall prepare a sacrifice of two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, a third of a hin.
And you shall present wine for a drink offering, a third of a hin, for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
But if you prepare an animal from the cattle for a whole burnt offering or for a sacrifice to honour a vow, or for a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord,
he shall present with the calf a sacrifice of three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, half a hin,
and half a hin of wine as a drink offering, an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
Thus you shall do for each calf, or each ram, or each lamb from the sheep or from the goats.
According to the number that you prepare, thus you shall do for each one according to their number.
Every native-born person shall do such things in this way when presenting offerings of sweet savour unto the Lord.

But if a sojourner who joins you in your land, or whosoever is among you throughout your generations, makes an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord, as you do, so shall the congregation do unto the Lord.
You shall have one law, both you and the sojourners joined unto you, an everlasting law throughout your generations. As you are, so shall the sojourner be before the Lord.
One law and one ordinance shall apply to you and the sojourner attached to you.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land whither I bring you,
then it shall be, when you eat of the loaves of the land, that you shall take a portion, a gift set apart unto the Lord.
As the firstfruits of your dough, you shall set apart a loaf for a portion set apart; as a portion from the threshing floor, so you shall take it,
the firstfruits of your dough; and you shall give unto the Lord a portion set apart throughout your generations.
But when you err, and do not carry out all these commandments which the Lord spoke unto Moses,
as the Lord commanded you through Moses, from the day the Lord gave command to you and onward throughout your generations,

And if it happened unintentionally, out of the congregation’s sight, the whole congregation shall prepare one unblemished calf from the cattle as a whole burnt offering of sweet savour unto the Lord, with its sacrifice and drink offering according to the ordinance, and one male goat for sin.

And the priest shall make atonement for the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, and they shall be forgiven, because it was unintentional. They have brought their gift, an offering unto the Lord for their sin, before the Lord for their unintentional acts.
And forgiveness shall extend throughout the whole congregation of the sons of Israel and to the sojourner attached to you, because it was unintentional for the whole people.
But if one soul sins unintentionally, he shall present one year-old female goat for sin.
And the priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person who acted unintentionally and sinned unintentionally, making atonement for that person.
For the native among the sons of Israel, and for the sojourner joined unto them, they shall have one law for whosoever acts unintentionally.
And the soul that acts with a presumptuous hand, whether of the natives or of the sojourners, provokes God; that soul shall be destroyed from his people,
because he treated the word of the Lord as worthless, and scattered His commandments. That soul shall surely be wiped out; his sin is upon him.
And while the sons of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
And those who found him gathering wood on the Sabbath day brought him unto Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.
And they placed him in custody, because they had not determined what they should do to him.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying: The man must certainly be put to death. Stone him with stones, all the congregation.
And the whole congregation brought him outside the camp, and the whole congregation stoned him with stones outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the Lord said unto Moses, saying:

Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Let them make for themselves fringes upon the corners of their garments throughout their generations; and you shall put a blue thread upon the fringes of the corners.

And it shall be among your fringes; and you shall see them, and remember all the commandments of the Lord, and do them; and you shall not turn aside after your thoughts and after your eyes, after which you go a whoring,
that you may remember and do all My commandments, and be holy unto your God.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord your God.
And Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, spoke, with Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, son of Reuben.
And they rose up before Moses, with two hundred fifty men of the sons of Israel, leaders of the congregation, members summoned to the council, men of renown.
They banded together against Moses and Aaron and said: Enough for you! The whole congregation, all of them, is holy, and the Lord is among them. Why do you rise up against the Lord’s congregation?
And when Moses heard, he fell on his face.

And he said to Korah and all his congregation, God has looked upon and known those who are His and those who are holy, and has brought them near to Himself. Those He chose for Himself He brought near to Himself.
Do this: take fire pans for yourselves, Korah and all his congregation.
And put fire on them and place incense on them before the Lord tomorrow. The man the Lord chooses shall be holy. Let that suffice for you, sons of Levi!
And Moses said to Korah: Listen to me, sons of Levi.

Is this too little for you, that the God of Israel distinguished you from Israel’s congregation and brought you near to Himself to perform the ministries of the Lord’s tent and stand before the congregation to serve them?
And He brought you near, and all your brethren, the sons of Levi, with you. Do you seek to serve as priests?
Thus you and all your congregation have gathered against God. As for Aaron, who is he, that you grumble against him?
And Moses sent to summon Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, but they said: We will not come up.
Is it too little that you brought us up from a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness, that you rule over us as a ruler?
Even if you had brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey and given us an allotment of land and vineyards, you would have gouged out those men’s eyes. We will not come up!
And Moses was deeply distressed and said unto the Lord: Do not attend to their sacrifice. I have taken no desirable possession from any of them, nor have I harmed any of them.
And Moses said to Korah: Consecrate your congregation, and be ready before the Lord tomorrow, you, they, and Aaron.
And each of you shall take his fire pan and place incense on it; each shall present his fire pan before the Lord, two hundred fifty fire pans. You and Aaron shall each bring his fire pan.
And each took his fire pan, put fire on it, and placed incense on it. Moses and Aaron stood beside the entrances of the Tent of Testimony.
And Korah gathered all his congregation against them beside the entrance of the Tent of Testimony, and the Lord’s glory appeared to the whole congregation.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Separate yourselves from the midst of this congregation, and I will consume them all at once.
And they fell on their faces and said: O God, God of the spirits and of all flesh, if one man sinned, will the Lord’s anger be against the whole congregation?
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak to the congregation, saying: Withdraw all around from Korah’s congregation.
And Moses rose and went to Dathan and Abiram, and all the elders of Israel went with him.
And he said to the congregation: Separate yourselves from the tents of these stubborn men. Touch none of their possessions, lest you perish with them in all their sin.
And they withdrew from around Korah’s tent. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood beside the entrances of their tents, with their wives, their children, and their baggage.
And Moses said: By this you shall know that the Lord sent me to do all these deeds, and that they did not come from myself.
If these men die the death of all people, and a visitation comes upon them according to the visitation of all people, then the Lord has not sent me.

But if the Lord displays a portent, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them, their households, their tents, and everything that belongs to them, and they go down alive to Hades, then you shall know that these men have provoked the Lord.
As he finished speaking all these words, the ground beneath them split apart.
And the earth opened and swallowed them, their households, all the people who were with Korah, and their livestock.
And they and all that belonged to them went down alive to Hades; the earth covered them, and they perished from the midst of the congregation.
And all Israel around them fled at their cry, saying: Lest the earth swallow us!
And fire went out from the Lord and consumed the two hundred fifty men presenting the incense.
And the Lord said unto Moses
and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest: Take up the bronze fire pans from among those burned up, and scatter this strange fire there, for they have consecrated

the fire pans of these sinners at the cost of their lives. Make them into hammered plates as a covering for the altar, because they were presented before the Lord and were made holy, and became a sign to the sons of Israel.
And Eleazar son of Aaron the priest took the bronze fire pans presented by those who had been burned, and they applied them as a covering for the altar,

as a reminder to the sons of Israel that no outsider who is not a descendant of Aaron should approach to place incense before the Lord, so that he will not become like Korah and his faction, as the Lord had spoken through Moses.
And the next day the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying: You have killed the Lord’s people!
And when the congregation banded together against Moses and Aaron, they rushed toward the Tent of Testimony. The cloud covered it, and the Lord’s glory appeared.
And Moses and Aaron came into the area before the Tent of Testimony.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Withdraw from the midst of this congregation, and I will consume them all at once. They fell on their faces.

And Moses said unto Aaron: Take the fire pan, put fire from the altar on it, and place incense on it. Carry it quickly into the camp and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from before the Lord; it has begun to strike the people.
And Aaron took it just as Moses had told him and ran into the congregation. The outbreak had already begun among the people. He placed the incense and made atonement for the people,
and stood between the dead and the living, and the outbreak subsided.
And those who died in the outbreak numbered fourteen thousand seven hundred, apart from those who died because of Korah.
And Aaron returned unto Moses at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony, and the outbreak subsided.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel and take from them one staff for each ancestral house, from all their leaders according to their ancestral houses—twelve staffs. Write each man’s name on his staff.
And write Aaron’s name on Levi’s staff, for they shall give one staff for each tribe of their ancestral houses.
And you shall place them in the Tent of Testimony, opposite the testimony, where I will make Myself known unto you.
And the staff of the man I choose shall sprout. I will remove from Myself the sons of Israel’s grumbling, which they direct against you.
And Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and all their leaders gave him staffs, one staff for each leader according to their ancestral houses—twelve staffs. Aaron’s staff was among their staffs.
And Moses placed the staffs before the Lord in the Tent of Testimony.
And the next day Moses and Aaron entered the Tent of Testimony, and there Aaron’s staff for the house of Levi had sprouted: it brought forth a shoot, flowered with blossoms, and produced nuts.
And Moses brought all the staffs out from before the Lord to all the sons of Israel. They looked, and each man took his staff.
And the Lord said unto Moses: Put Aaron’s staff before the testimonies, to be kept as a sign for the sons of the disobedient. Let their grumbling against Me cease, and they shall certainly not die.
And Moses and Aaron did so. Just as the Lord commanded Moses, so they did.
And the sons of Israel said unto Moses: Behold, we are consumed! We are lost! We are utterly spent!
Everyone who touches the Lord’s tent dies. Must we die to the very end?
And the Lord said unto Aaron, saying: You and your sons and your father’s house shall bear the sins concerning the holy things; and you and your sons shall bear the sins concerning your priesthood.
And bring your brethren, the tribe of Levi, your father’s clan, near unto you; and let them join you and minister unto you; and you and your sons with you shall be before the Tent of Testimony.
And they shall keep your charges and the charges of the Tent; only they shall not approach the holy vessels and the altar, that neither they nor you may die.
And they shall join you, and shall keep the charges of the Tent of Testimony according to all the ministries of the Tent; and the outsider shall not approach you.
And you shall keep the charges of the holy things and the charges of the altar, and there shall be no wrath among the sons of Israel.
And I have taken your brothers the Levites from among the sons of Israel, a gift given unto the Lord, to perform the ministries of the Tent of Testimony.

And you and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood in every matter of the altar and within the veil; and you shall perform the ministries, a gift of your priesthood; and the outsider who approaches shall die.

And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: And I, behold, have given you charge of the firstfruits; from all things sanctified unto Me by the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you for a share of honour, and unto your sons after you, an everlasting ordinance.

And this shall be yours from the consecrated holy offerings: from all their gifts, and from all their sacrifices, and from every guilt offering of theirs, and from all their sin offerings which they render unto Me; from all the holy things it shall be yours and your sons’.
You shall eat them in the most holy place; every male shall eat them, you and your sons; they shall be holy unto you.

And this shall be yours, the firstfruits of their gifts: from all the presentations of the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance. Everyone clean in your house shall eat them.
Every firstfruit of oil, and every firstfruit of wine and grain, their firstfruits which they give unto the Lord, I have given them unto you.
All the first produce in their land, which they bring unto the Lord, shall be yours; everyone clean in your house shall eat it.
Everything devoted among the sons of Israel shall be yours.

And everything that opens the womb of all flesh, which they present unto the Lord, from man unto livestock, shall be yours; but the firstborn of men shall surely be redeemed, and you shall redeem the firstborn of unclean livestock.
And its redemption shall be from one month old; the valuation is five shekels by the holy shekel, which is twenty obols.

But you shall not redeem the firstborn of calves, and the firstborn of sheep, and the firstborn of goats; they are holy. And you shall pour their blood against the altar, and you shall offer up the fat as an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
And their flesh shall be yours; as the breast of the presentation and the right foreleg, it shall be yours.

Every portion of the holy things which the sons of Israel set apart unto the Lord I have given unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance; it is a covenant of everlasting salt before the Lord for you and for your seed after you.
And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: You shall not inherit in their land, neither shall you have a portion among them; for I am your portion and your inheritance among the sons of Israel.
And to the sons of Levi, look, I have given every tithe in Israel as an allotment in return for their ministries, the service they perform in the Tent of Testimony.
And the sons of Israel shall no longer approach the Tent of Testimony, incurring a death-bringing sin.

And the Levite himself shall perform the ministry of the Tent of Testimony, and they shall bear their offences. It is an everlasting ordinance throughout their generations. Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no inheritance.

For the tithes of the sons of Israel that they set apart for the Lord as a portion set apart I have given to the Levites as an allotment. Therefore I have said to them: Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no allotment.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

And you shall speak unto the Levites, and shall say unto them: When you receive from the sons of Israel the tithe which I have given you from them for an allotment, you shall take from it a portion set apart unto the Lord, a tithe of the tithe.
And your portions set apart shall be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing floor and as a portion set apart from the winepress.

Thus you shall also take of the portions set apart unto the Lord, from all your tithes which you receive from the sons of Israel; and from them you shall give a portion set apart unto the Lord unto Aaron the priest.
From all your gifts you shall take a portion set apart unto the Lord, or from all the firstfruits the consecrated portion thereof.
And you shall say unto them: When you take the firstfruits from it, it shall be reckoned unto the Levites as produce from the threshing floor and as produce from the winepress.
And you shall eat it in every place, you and your households, for it is your wage in return for your ministries in the Tent of Testimony.
And you shall incur no sin through it, when you take the firstfruits from it; and you shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel, lest you die.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:

This is the provision of the law which the Lord commanded, saying: Speak unto the sons of Israel, and let them bring unto you a red heifer without blemish, wherein is no defect, and upon which no yoke has been laid.
And you shall give it unto Eleazar the priest, and they shall bring it outside the camp unto a clean place, and shall slaughter it before him.
And Eleazar shall take some of its blood and sprinkle some of its blood seven times toward the front of the Tent of Testimony.
And they shall burn it before him; its skin, flesh, and blood, together with its dung, shall be burned.
And the priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet material, and they shall throw them into the burning heifer.
And the priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Afterward he may enter the camp, but the priest shall be unclean until evening.
And the one who burns it shall wash his clothes and bathe his body, and he shall be unclean until evening.

And a clean person shall gather the heifer's ashes and deposit them outside the camp in a clean place. They shall be kept for the congregation of the sons of Israel as water of sprinkling; it is a means of purification.
And the one who gathers the heifer's ashes shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. This shall be an everlasting ordinance for the sons of Israel and the attached sojourners.
Whosoever touches a dead person, any human being who has died, shall be unclean for seven days.
That person shall be purified on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean. If he is not purified on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be clean.

Whosoever touches the dead body of any human being who has died, and is not purified, has defiled the Tent of the Lord; that soul shall be wiped out from Israel. Because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still in him.
And this is the law: If a person dies in a house, everyone who enters the house and everything in the house shall be unclean for seven days.
And every open vessel without a fastening tied upon it is unclean.
And anyone who touches, on the open plain, one slain, a dead person, a human bone, or a tomb shall be unclean for seven days.
And for the unclean person they shall take some ashes from what was burned for purification, and they shall pour living water over them into a vessel.

And a clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it around the house, the vessels, and the people who were there, and on whoever touched the human bone, the slain person, the dead person, or the tomb.

And the clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. He shall be purified on the seventh day, wash his clothes, and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.

And if a man is defiled, and is not purified, that soul shall be destroyed from the midst of the congregation, because he has defiled the holy things of the Lord; because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean.
And this shall be an everlasting ordinance for you. The one who sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes, and whosoever touches the water of sprinkling shall be unclean until evening.
And whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.
And the sons of Israel, the whole congregation, came into the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people remained at Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.
And there was no water for the congregation, and they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
And the people reviled Moses, saying: If only we had died when our brothers were destroyed before the Lord!
And why have you brought the Lord's congregation into this wilderness to kill us and our livestock?
And why have you brought us up from Egypt to arrive at this wretched place—a place where nothing is sown, with no figs, vines, pomegranates, or water to drink?
And Moses and Aaron went away from the congregation to the entrance of the Tent of Testimony and fell on their faces. The Lord's glory appeared to them.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Take the staff, and gather the congregation, you and Aaron your brother; and speak unto the rock before them, and it shall give its waters; and you shall bring water out of the rock for them, and shall give the congregation and their livestock to drink.
And Moses took the staff that was before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded.
And Moses and Aaron assembled the congregation before the rock. He said to them: Listen to me, you disobedient people! Surely we are not to bring water out of this rock for you?
And Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with the staff. Abundant water came out, and the congregation and their livestock drank.
And the Lord said unto Moses and Aaron: Because you did not believe so as to show Me holy before the sons of Israel, you shall not bring this congregation into the land that I have given them.
This is the Water of Dispute, because the sons of Israel reviled before the Lord, and He was shown holy among them.
And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom, saying: Thus says your brother Israel: You know all the hardship that has overtaken us.
And our fathers went down to Egypt, and we lived as sojourners in Egypt many days. The Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers.
And we cried out unto the Lord, and the Lord heard our voice; He sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are at Kadesh, a town at the edge of your territory.

We will pass through your land. We will not cross fields or vineyards or drink water from your cistern. We will travel the royal road and turn neither right nor left until we have passed through your territory.
And Edom said to him: You shall not pass through me; otherwise I will come out to meet you in war.

And the sons of Israel say unto him: We will pass alongside the mountain. If I and the livestock drink your water, I will pay you its price. The matter is nothing; we will pass alongside the mountain.
He said: You shall not pass through me. Edom came out to meet him with a large force and a strong hand.
And Edom was unwilling to allow Israel to pass through his territory, so Israel turned away from him.
And they set out from Kadesh, and the sons of Israel, the whole congregation, arrived at Mount Hor.
And the Lord said unto Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom:
Let Aaron be gathered to his people, for you shall certainly not enter the land that I have given to the sons of Israel, because you provoked Me at the Water of Reviling.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor before the whole congregation.
And strip Aaron of his robe and clothe his son Eleazar. Let Aaron be gathered and die there.
And Moses did as the Lord commanded, and he brought him up Mount Hor before the whole congregation.
And he stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron died on the summit of the mountain, and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
And the whole congregation saw that Aaron had been released, and all the house of Israel wept for Aaron thirty days.
And the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived by the wilderness, heard—for Israel had come by the road of Atharim—and fought Israel, and they took captives from them.
And Israel vowed a vow unto the Lord: If Thou hand this people over into my power, I will devote them and their towns to destruction.
And the Lord heard Israel's voice and handed the Canaanite over into his power. Israel devoted him and his towns to destruction, and they called that place Devotion to Destruction.
And they set out from Mount Hor by the road toward the Red Sea and went around the land of Edom. The people became fainthearted on the journey.
And the people spoke against God and against Moses: Why have you brought us out of Egypt to kill us in the wilderness? There is no bread or water, and our soul is disgusted with this empty bread.
And the Lord sent deadly serpents among the people. They bit the people, and many of the sons of Israel died.

And the people came unto Moses and said: We have sinned by speaking against the Lord and against you. Therefore pray unto the Lord, and let Him remove the serpents from us. Moses prayed unto the Lord for the people.
And the Lord said unto Moses: Make a serpent for yourself, and set it upon a standard; and it shall be, if a serpent bites a man, that everyone bitten, when he looks upon it, shall live.
And Moses made a bronze serpent and set it on a standard. Whenever a serpent bit a person, that person looked at the bronze serpent and lived.
And the sons of Israel set out and camped at Oboth.
And they set out from Oboth and camped at Achel-gai, on the farther side, in the wilderness opposite Moab toward the sunrise.
From there they set out and camped in the ravine of Zered.
And from there they set out and camped beyond the Arnon, in the wilderness extending from the Amorite borders. The Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
Therefore it is said in a book: A war of the Lord set Zoob ablaze, and the torrents of the Arnon,
and he appointed the torrents for the settlement of Er, and it lies beside the borders of Moab.
And from there they went to the well. This is the well of which the Lord said unto Moses: Gather the people, and I will give them water to drink.
Then Israel sang this song over the well: Lead the singing for it!
A well: rulers dug it; kings of nations hewed it out in their kingdom, when they exercised dominion. From the well they went to Manthanain.
And from Manthanain they went to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth.
And from Bamoth they went to a valley in the plain of Moab, from the summit of the Hewn Height overlooking the wilderness.
And Moses sent envoys to Sihon king of the Amorites with words of peace, saying:

We will pass through your land; we will travel by the road. We will not turn aside into fields or vineyards or drink water from your well. We will travel the royal road until we have passed through your territory.

And Sihon would not allow Israel to pass through his territory. He gathered all his people and went out into the wilderness to array himself against Israel. He came to Jahaz and arrayed himself against Israel.
And Israel struck him by slaughter with the sword, and they took control of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the sons of Ammon, because Jazer is the border of the sons of Ammon.
And Israel took all these towns and settled in all the Amorite towns, in Heshbon and all the towns adjoining it.
Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had previously fought the king of Moab, and they took all his land from Aroer as far as the Arnon.
Therefore those who speak in riddles will say: Come to Heshbon, so that Sihon's city may be built and prepared.
For fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from Sihon's city. It consumed as far as Moab and swallowed the pillars of the Arnon.
Woe unto you, Moab! You are ruined, people of Chemosh. Their sons were handed over to escape, and their daughters as captives to Sihon king of the Amorites.
And their seed shall perish, from Heshbon as far as Dibon; and the women kindled still more fire against Moab.
Israel settled in all the towns of the Amorites.
And Moses sent men to inspect Jazer. They captured it and its villages and drove out the Amorites who lived there.
And they turned and went up by the road to Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out to meet them with all his people, for battle at Edrei.

And the Lord said unto Moses: Do not fear him, for I have handed him, all his people, and all his land into your hands. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.
And he struck him, and his sons, and all his people, until he left none of his alive; and they inherited their land.
And the sons of Israel set out and camped on the western side of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho.
And Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
And Moab was very afraid of the people because they were numerous; Moab was distressed by the sons of Israel.

And Moab said to the council of elders of Midian: Now this congregation will lick up everyone around us as a calf licks up the green plants of the plain. Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

And he sent envoys to Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, beside the river in the land of his people, to summon him: Behold, a people has come out of Egypt. They cover the face of the land and are encamped next to me.

And now come and curse this people for me, for they are stronger than we are. If we can strike some of them, I will drive them from the land. I know that those you bless are blessed, and those you curse are cursed.
And the council of elders of Moab and the council of elders of Midian went with the means of divination in their hands. They came to Balaam and told him Balak's words.
And he said to them: Lodge here for the night, and I will answer you with whatever the Lord speaks to me. The officials of Moab remained with Balaam.
And God came to Balaam and said to him: Who are these men with you?
And Balaam said to God: Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent them to me, saying:
Behold, a people has come out of Egypt and covers the face of the land; they are encamped next to me. Now come and curse them for me. Perhaps I can strike them and drive them from the land.
And God said to Balaam: You shall not go with them or curse the people, for they are blessed.
And Balaam rose in the morning and said to Balak's officials: Hurry back to your lord, for God does not permit me to go with you.
And the officials of Moab rose, came to Balak, and said: Balaam is unwilling to come with us.
And Balak again sent officials, more numerous and more honoured than these.
And they came to Balaam and say unto him: Thus says Balak son of Zippor: I ask you, do not hesitate to come to me.
I will honour you richly, and I will do for you whatever you say. Come and curse this people for me.

And Balaam answered Balak's officials: Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not transgress the word of the Lord God to do anything small or great according to my own intention.
And now you also remain here tonight, and I will learn what more the Lord will say to me.
And God came to Balaam at night and said to him: If these men are here to summon you, rise and follow them. But you shall do what I tell you.
And Balaam rose in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the officials of Moab.
And God grew angry because he went. God's angel rose to obstruct him. Balaam was riding his donkey, with his two servants beside him.
And the donkey saw God's angel opposing them in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. She turned off the road into the plain, and he struck her with the staff to direct her onto the road.
And God's angel stood in the furrows of the vineyards, with a fence on either side.
And the donkey saw God's angel and pressed herself against the wall, crushing Balaam's foot. He whipped her again.
And God's angel went farther and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn right or left.
And the donkey saw God's angel and crouched beneath Balaam. Balaam became angry and beat the donkey with his staff.
And God opened the donkey's mouth, and she says to Balaam: What have I done unto you that you have struck me this third time?
And Balaam said to the donkey: Because you have mocked me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would have stabbed you already.
And the donkey says to Balaam: Am I not your donkey, which you have ridden from your youth until this day? Have I acted like this toward you out of deliberate disregard? He said: No.
God uncovered Balaam's eyes, and he sees the Lord's angel opposing him in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. He bent down and prostrated himself on his face.
And God's angel said to him: Why have you struck your donkey this third time? Behold, I have come out to oppose you, because your way is not fitting before me.
And the donkey saw me and turned away from me this third time. If she had not turned away, I would now have killed you and preserved her.
And Balaam said unto the Lord's angel: I have sinned, for I did not know that you were opposing me in the road. Now, if this does not please you, I will turn back.
And God's angel said to Balaam: Go with the men, but take care to speak the word that I tell you. Balaam went with Balak's officials.
And Balak heard that Balaam had arrived and went out to meet him at a city of Moab on the Arnon border, at the edge of the territory.
And Balak said to Balaam: Did I not send to summon you? Why did you not come to me? Am I really unable to honour you?
And Balaam said to Balak: Behold, I have come unto you. Am I now able to say anything? I shall speak the word that God puts in my mouth.
And Balaam went with Balak, and they came to towns of farmsteads.
And Balak sacrificed sheep and calves and sent portions to Balaam and the officials with him.
And in the morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Baal's pillar. From there he showed him a part of the people.
And Balaam said to Balak: Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven calves and seven rams for me here.
And Balak did as Balaam told him, and he offered a calf and a ram on each altar.

And Balaam said to Balak: Stand beside your sacrifice, while I go to see whether God will appear to meet me. Whatever He shows me, I will tell you. Balak stood beside his sacrifice, and Balaam went to inquire of God; he went straight on.
And God appeared to Balaam, and Balaam said to Him: I have prepared the seven altars and offered a calf and a ram on each altar.
And God put a word in Balaam's mouth and said: Return to Balak and thus you shall speak.
And he returned to him, and there he stood beside his whole burnt offerings, with all the officials of Moab.

And God's Spirit came upon him, and he took up his parable and said: Balak summoned me from Mesopotamia, the king of Moab from the eastern mountains: Come, curse Jacob for me; come, call down a curse on Israel for me.
Why should I curse whom the Lord does not curse? Why should I call down a curse on whom God does not curse?
From the tops of mountains I shall see them, and from the hills I shall observe them. Behold, a people who will dwell alone, not counted among the nations.
Who has measured Jacob’s seed exactly, and who will count Israel's clans? May my soul die among righteous souls, and may my seed be like their seed!
And Balak said to Balaam: What have you done to me? I summoned you to curse my enemies, and look, you have pronounced a blessing!
And Balaam said to Balak: Must I not take care to speak what God puts in my mouth?
And Balak said to him: Come with me to another place, from which you shall not see them except for a part; you shall in no wise see them all. Curse them for me from there.
And he took him to a lookout in a field, to the summit of the Hewn Height, built seven altars there, and offered a calf and a ram on each altar.
And Balaam said to Balak: Stand beside your sacrifice, while I go to inquire of God.
And God met Balaam, put a word in his mouth, and said: Return to Balak and speak these words.
And he returned to him, and there he stood beside his whole burning, with all the officials of Moab. Balak said to him: What did the Lord say?
And he took up his parable and said: Rise, Balak, and hear! Listen as a witness, son of Zippor!
God is not as a man, to be led astray, nor as a son of man, to be threatened; having spoken, shall He not act? Shall He speak, and not abide by it?
Behold, I have been taken up to bless. I will bless and certainly will not reverse it.
There shall be no toil in Jacob, neither shall distress be seen in Israel; the Lord his God is with him; the glories of rulers are in him.
God brought them out of Egypt; his glory is as that of a one-horned beast.
There is no omen-taking in Jacob and no divination in Israel. At the appointed time it shall be said to Jacob and Israel what God will accomplish.
Behold, a people will rise like a lion cub and exult like a lion. It will not sleep until it eats prey and drinks the blood of the slain.
And Balak said to Balaam: Neither curse them for me nor bless them at all!
And Balaam answered Balak: Did I not tell you that I must do the word that God speaks?
And Balak said to Balaam: Come; I will take you to another place. If it pleases God, curse them for me from there.
And Balak took Balaam to the summit of Peor, which extends toward the wilderness.
And Balaam said to Balak: Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven calves and seven rams for me here.
And Balak did as Balaam told him and offered a calf and a ram on each altar.
And Balaam saw that it was good before the Lord to bless Israel, so he did not go as usual to seek omens. He turned his face toward the wilderness.
And Balaam raised his eyes and sees Israel encamped by tribes, and God's Spirit came within him.
And he took up his parable and said: Balaam son of Beor declares; the man who sees truly declares,
one who hears God's oracles declares, who saw a vision of God in sleep, with his eyes uncovered:
How beautiful are your houses, Jacob, your tents, Israel!
Like shaded wooded valleys, like gardens beside rivers, like tents pitched by the Lord, like cedars beside waters.
A man shall come forth from his seed and rule over many nations. His kingdom shall rise higher than Gog, and his kingdom shall increase.
God guided him out of Egypt; his glory is like a one-horned beast's. He shall devour the nations of his enemies, suck the marrow from their fat parts, and shoot down an enemy with his missiles.
He lay down and rested like a lion, like a lion cub—who will rouse him? Those who bless you are blessed, and those who curse you are cursed.
And Balak became angry with Balaam and clapped his hands. He said to Balaam: I summoned you to curse my enemy, and look, you have thoroughly blessed them this third time!
Now flee to your own place! I said I would honour you, but now the Lord has deprived you of glory.
And Balaam said to Balak: Did I not tell the messengers whom you sent to me:
Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not transgress the Lord's word to do evil or good on my own. Whatever God says, I must say.
And now look, I am returning to my place. Come, I will advise you what this people will do to your people at the end of the days.
And he took up his parable and said: Balaam son of Beor declares; the man who sees truly declares,
one who hears God's oracles, who knows knowledge from the Most High and has seen a vision of God in sleep, with his eyes uncovered:

I will show him, but not now; I pronounce him blessed, but he does not draw near. A star shall rise from Jacob, and a man shall arise from Israel. He shall crush Moab's leaders and plunder all the sons of Seth.
And Edom shall become an inheritance, and Esau, his enemy, shall become an inheritance; Israel acted with strength.
And one shall arise from Jacob and destroy whoever escapes from a city.
And he saw Amalek, took up his parable, and said: Amalek is the beginning of nations, and their seed shall perish.
And he saw the Kenite, took up his parable, and said: Your dwelling is strong; even if you set your nest in a rock,
And even if a nest of craftiness should belong to Beor, Assyrians shall take you captive.
And he saw Og, took up his parable, and said: Alas, alas! Who will live when God brings these things about?
And one shall come forth from the hand of the Kitians, and they shall afflict Asshur and the Hebrews; they themselves shall perish together.
And Balaam rose and departed, returning to his place, and Balak went home.
And Israel lodged at Shittim, and the people profaned themselves by engaging in sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab.
And they invited them to the sacrifices of their idols. The people ate from their sacrifices and bowed down to their idols.
And Israel was initiated into the worship of Baal of Peor, and the Lord became angry with Israel.
And the Lord said unto Moses: Take all the leaders of the people and make a public example of them before the Lord in the sunlight, and the Lord's fierce anger will turn away from Israel.
And Moses said to Israel's tribes: Each of you shall kill his own kinsman who was initiated into the worship of Baal of Peor.

And an Israelite man came and brought his brother to the Midianite woman before Moses and the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, while they were weeping at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.
And Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw it, rose from among the congregation, and took a lance in his hand.
He went after the Israelite man into the chamber and stabbed both of them, the Israelite man and the woman, through her womb. The plague against the sons of Israel stopped.
And those who died in the plague numbered twenty-four thousand.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has stopped My wrath against the sons of Israel by being zealous with My zeal among them, and I did not consume the sons of Israel in My zeal.
Therefore say: Behold, I give him a covenant of peace.
And it shall be for him and his seed after him an everlasting covenant of priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the sons of Israel.
The name of the Israelite man struck down with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, a ruler of an ancestral house of Simeon.
And the name of the Midianite woman who was struck down was Cozbi daughter of Zur, a ruler of the nation of Ommoth, an ancestral house of Midian.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel, saying:
Be hostile to the Midianites and strike them,

for they are hostile to you through the deceit by which they deceive you because of Peor and because of Cozbi, daughter of a Midianite ruler, their sister, who was struck down on the day of the plague because of Peor.
And after the plague, the Lord spoke unto Moses and Eleazar the priest:
Take the sum of the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, from twenty years old and upward, by their ancestral houses, everyone who goes out to line up for battle in Israel.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke in Araboth of Moab beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying:
From twenty years old and upward, as the Lord commanded Moses. These are the sons of Israel who came out of Egypt:
Reuben was Israel's firstborn. The sons of Reuben: Hanoch and the clan of Hanoch; from Pallu, the clan of Pallu;
from Hezron, the clan of Hezron; from Carmi, the clan of Carmi.
These were Reuben's clans. Their registration numbered forty-three thousand seven hundred thirty.
And the sons of Pallu: Eliab.

And the sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These were summoned members of the congregation, those who rose against Moses and Aaron in Korah's congregation in the uprising against the Lord.
And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and Korah when his congregation died, when the fire consumed the two hundred fifty; they became a sign.
But Korah's sons did not die.
And the sons of Simeon, the clan of the sons of Simeon: from Nemuel, the clan of Nemuel; from Jamin, the clan of Jamin; from Jachin, the clan of Jachin;
from Zerah, the clan of Zerah; from Shaul, the clan of Shaul.
These were Simeon's clans according to their registration: twenty-two thousand two hundred.
The sons of Judah were Er and Onan. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
The sons of Judah by their clans: from Shelon, the clan of Shelon; from Perez, the clan of Perez; from Zerah, the clan of Zerah.
And the sons of Perez: from Hezron, the clan of Hezron; from Iamun, the clan of Iamun.
These were Judah's clans according to their registration: seventy-six thousand five hundred.
And the sons of Issachar by their clans: from Tola, the clan of Tola; from Puah, the clan of Puah;
from Jashub, the clan of Jashub; from Shimron, the clan of Shimron.
These were Issachar's clans according to their registration: sixty-four thousand three hundred.
The sons of Zebulun by their clans: from Sered, the clan of Sered; from Allon, the clan of Allon; from Allel, the clan of Allel.
These were Zebulun's clans according to their registration: sixty thousand five hundred.
The sons of Gad by their clans: from Zephon, the clan of Zephon; from Haggi, the clan of Haggi; from Shuni, the clan of Shuni;
from Ozni, the clan of Ozni; from Addi, the clan of Addi;
from Arod, the clan of Arod; from Ariel, the clan of Ariel.
These were the clans of the sons of Gad according to their registration: forty thousand five hundred.
The sons of Asher by their clans: from Jamin, the clan of Jamin; from Ishvi, the clan of Ishvi; from Beriah, the clan of Beriah;
from Heber, the clan of Heber; from Malchiel, the clan of Malchiel.
And the name of Asher's daughter was Sarah.
These were Asher's clans according to their registration: fifty-three thousand four hundred.
The sons of Joseph by their clans were Manasseh and Ephraim.
The sons of Manasseh: from Machir, the clan of Machir. Machir begat Gilead; from Gilead, the clan of Gilead.
And these were the sons of Gilead: from Ahiezer, the clan of Ahiezer; from Helek, the clan of Helek;
from Esriel, the clan of Esriel; from Shechem, the clan of Shechem;
from Symaer, the clan of Symaer; from Hepher, the clan of Hepher.
And Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters. These were the names of Zelophehad's daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These were Manasseh's clans according to their registration: fifty-two thousand seven hundred.
And these were the sons of Ephraim: from Shuthelah, the clan of Shuthelah; from Tanach, the clan of Tanach.
These were the sons of Shuthelah: from Eden, the clan of Eden.
These were Ephraim's clans according to their registration: thirty-two thousand five hundred. These were the clans of the sons of Joseph by their clans.
The sons of Benjamin by their clans: from Bela, the clan of Bela; from Asyber, the clan of Asyber; from Iachiran, the clan of Iachiran;
from Sophan, the clan of Sophan.
And the sons of Bela were Adar and Naaman: from Adar, the clan of Adar; from Naaman, the clan of Naaman.
These were the sons of Benjamin by their clans according to their registration: forty-five thousand six hundred.
And the sons of Dan by their clans: from Sami, the clan of Sami. These were Dan's clans by their families.
All the clans of Sami according to their registration numbered sixty-four thousand four hundred.
The sons of Naphtali by their clans: from Asiel, the clan of Asiel; from Guni, the clan of Guni;
from Jezer, the clan of Jezer; from Shillem, the clan of Shillem.
These were Naphtali's clans according to their registration: forty-five thousand four hundred.
The registration of the sons of Israel numbered six hundred one thousand seven hundred thirty.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
The land shall be divided among these for inheritance according to the number of names.
To the more numerous you shall increase the inheritance, and to the fewer you shall reduce their inheritance. Each shall receive its inheritance according to their registration.
The land shall be divided by lots. They shall inherit according to the names of their ancestral tribes.
You shall divide their inheritance by the lot between the more numerous and the fewer.
And the sons of Levi by their clans: from Gershon, the clan of Gershon; from Kohath, the clan of Kohath; from Merari, the clan of Merari.
These were the clans of the sons of Levi: the clan of Libni, the clan of Hebron, the clan of Korah, and the clan of Mushi. Kohath begat Amram.
And his wife was named Jochebed, a daughter of Levi, who bore these to Levi in Egypt. She bore Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam to Amram.
And to Aaron were born Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
And Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai.

And those registered numbered twenty-three thousand, every male from one month old and upward. They were not registered together with the sons of Israel, because no allotment is given to them among the sons of Israel.
And this was the registration by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who registered the sons of Israel in Araboth of Moab beside the Jordan opposite Jericho.
And among these there was no man from those registered by Moses and Aaron, when they registered the sons of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai.
For the Lord had said of them: They shall certainly die in the wilderness. Not one of them remained except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
And the daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, of the clan of Manasseh among the sons of Joseph, came forward. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
And they stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the rulers, and the whole congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony, saying:
Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the congregation that rose against the Lord in Korah's congregation; he died because of his own sin, and he had no sons.
Let our father's name not be erased from his clan because he has no son. Give us a possession among our father's brothers.
And Moses brought their case before the Lord.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
The daughters of Zelophehad have spoken rightly. You shall surely give them a possession of inheritance among their father’s brethren, and shall assign their father’s allotment unto them.
And you shall speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: If a man dies, and has no son, you shall assign his inheritance unto his daughter.
But if he has no daughter, you shall give the inheritance to his brother.
But if he has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his father's brother.

But if his father has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his nearest relative from his tribe, and he shall inherit his property. This shall be a rule of judgment for the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And the Lord said unto Moses: Go up the mountain on the farther side—this is Mount Nebo—and see the land of Canaan that I am giving to the sons of Israel as a possession.
And you shall see it, and you also shall be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was gathered at Mount Hor,

because you transgressed My word in the wilderness of Zin during the congregation’s resistance, when you were to sanctify Me; you did not sanctify Me at the water before them. This is the Water of Dispute at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.
And Moses said unto the Lord:
Let the Lord, the God of spirits and of all flesh, appoint a man over this congregation,
who will go out before them and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the Lord's congregation will not be like sheep without a shepherd.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying: Take unto yourself Joshua son of Nun, a man who has spirit within him, and you shall lay your hands upon him,
and shall set him before Eleazar the priest, and shall instruct him before all the congregation, and shall give instructions concerning him before them,
and shall put of your glory upon him, that the sons of Israel may obey him.

And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, and they shall ask him for the judgment of the manifestations before the Lord. At his word they shall go out, and at his word they shall come in: he, the sons of Israel together, and the whole congregation.
And Moses did as the Lord commanded him. He took Joshua and stood him before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation.
And he laid his hands on him and presented him, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Command the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them, saying: You shall take care to present My gifts, My donations, My offerings of sweet savour unto Me at My feasts.
And you shall say unto them: These are the offerings which you shall bring unto the Lord: two unblemished year-old lambs each day for a continual whole burning;
you shall offer the one lamb in the morning, and you shall offer the second lamb toward evening.
And you shall prepare a tenth of an oiphi of fine flour for a sacrifice, mixed with oil, a fourth of a hin.
It is a continual whole burnt offering, instituted at Mount Sinai as a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And its drink offering shall be a fourth of a hin for each lamb; in the holy place you shall pour out a drink offering of strong drink unto the Lord.
And you shall offer the second lamb toward evening; you shall prepare it according to its sacrifice and according to its drink offering for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And on the Sabbath day you shall bring two unblemished year-old lambs, and two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice, and a drink offering,
a Sabbath whole burnt offering on each Sabbath, besides the continual whole burning and its drink offering.
And at the new moons you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord: two calves from the cattle, and one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs;
For each calf, three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil; for each ram, two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil;
For each lamb, a tenth of fine flour mixed with oil: a sacrifice, a sweet savour, an offering unto the Lord.
Their drink offering shall be wine: half a hin for each calf, a third of a hin for each ram, and a quarter of a hin for each lamb. This is the whole burnt offering month by month throughout the year.
And one male goat from the goats for sin unto the Lord; besides the continual whole burning shall it be offered, and its drink offering.
And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is the Lord's Passover.
And on the fifteenth day of this month is a festival. You shall eat unleavened bread for seven days.
And the first day shall be a holy appointed assembly for you. You shall do no laborious work.
And you shall bring whole burnt offerings, offerings unto the Lord: two calves from the cattle, one ram, seven year-old lambs; they shall be unblemished for you.
And their sacrifice shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each calf and two tenths for each ram.
You shall prepare a tenth for each lamb, for the seven lambs;
And offer one male goat for sin, to make atonement for you,
besides the continual morning whole burning, which is a continual whole burnt offering.
These you shall prepare in this manner each day for seven days, a gift, an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord; besides the continual whole burnt offering you shall prepare its drink offering.
And the seventh day shall be a holy summoned assembly for you. You shall do no laborious work on it.
And on the day of new produce, when you present a new sacrifice unto the Lord at the festival of weeks, you shall have a holy appointed assembly. You shall do no laborious work.
And you shall bring whole burnt offerings for a sweet savour unto the Lord: two calves from the cattle, one ram, seven unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifice shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each calf and two tenths for each ram;
a tenth for each of the seven lambs;
and one male goat for sin, to make atonement for you.
These are apart from the continual whole burnt offering. You shall prepare their sacrifice for Me—they shall be unblemished—and their drink offerings.
And in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall hold a holy appointed assembly. You shall do no laborious work. It shall be a day of signalling for you.
And you shall present whole burnt offerings as a sweet savour unto the Lord: one calf from the cattle, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifice shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the calf and two tenths for the ram,
and one tenth for each of the seven lambs.
And also offer one male goat for sin, to make atonement for you,

besides the whole burnt offerings of the new moon, their sacrifices and their drink offerings, and the continual whole burnt offerings, their sacrifices and their drink offerings, according to their prescription, as a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And on the tenth day of this month you shall have a holy appointed assembly; and you shall afflict your souls, and shall do no work.
And you shall present whole burnt offerings as a sweet savour unto the Lord, offerings: one calf from the cattle, one ram, and seven year-old lambs; they shall be unblemished for you.
Their sacrifice shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the calf and two tenths for the one ram,
and one tenth for each of the seven lambs.

And also offer one male goat for sin, to make atonement for you, besides the sin offering of atonement, the continual whole burning, its sacrifice and its drink offering, according to the prescription, as a sweet savour, an offering unto the Lord.
And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month you shall hold a holy appointed assembly. You shall do no laborious work and shall keep a festival unto the Lord for seven days.

And on the first day you shall present whole burnt offerings, offerings, as a sweet savour unto the Lord: thirteen calves from the cattle, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs; they shall be unblemished.
Their sacrifices shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each of the thirteen calves and two tenths for each of the two rams,
and one tenth for each of the fourteen lambs.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
And on the second day offer twelve calves from the cattle, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifice and their drink offering for the calves, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
On the third day offer eleven calves, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifice and their drink offering for the calves, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
On the fourth day offer ten calves, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifices and their drink offerings for the calves, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
On the fifth day offer nine calves, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifices and their drink offerings for the calves, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
On the sixth day offer eight calves, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifices and their drink offerings for the calves, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
On the seventh day offer seven calves, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifices and their drink offerings for the calves, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, according to their prescription.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
And on the eighth day you shall hold a closing festival. You shall do no laborious work on it.
And you shall present whole burnt offerings as a sweet savour, offerings unto the Lord: one calf, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifices and their drink offerings for the calf, the ram, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.

You shall offer these unto the Lord at your festivals, apart from your vows, your freewill offerings, your whole burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your drink offerings, and your sacrifices of deliverance.
And Moses told the sons of Israel everything that the Lord had commanded Moses.
And Moses spoke to the rulers of the tribes of Israel, saying: This is the word that the Lord has commanded:
Any person who vows a vow unto the Lord, or swears an oath, or imposes a restriction upon himself, shall not profane his word. He shall do everything that comes from his mouth.
If a woman vows a vow unto the Lord or imposes a restriction while in her father’s house in her youth,

and her father hears her vows and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself, but her father remains silent toward her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain.
But if her father refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall stand. The Lord will cleanse her, because her father refused her.
If she becomes a man’s wife while her vows are upon her, according to the specific statement of her lips by which she imposed a restriction upon herself,
and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her on the day he hears, then all her vows shall stand, and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain.
But if her husband refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain, because her husband refused her. The Lord will cleanse her.
And the vow of a widow or a divorced woman—whatever she vowed concerning herself—shall remain against her.
If her vow was made in her husband’s house, or her restriction was imposed upon herself with an oath,
and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her, and does not refuse her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions which she imposed upon her soul shall stand against her.
