But if her husband utterly annuls them on the day he hears, then whatever came from her lips concerning her vows and the restrictions upon herself shall not remain against her. Her husband has annulled them, and the Lord will cleanse her.
Every vow and every oath imposing a restriction to afflict her soul—her husband may establish it, or her husband may annul it.

But if he remains utterly silent toward her from day to day, he shall establish all her vows, and he shall establish the restrictions upon her, because he kept silence toward her on the day when he heard.
But if he annuls them after the day on which he heard, he shall bear his sin.
These are the ordinances that the Lord commanded Moses between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter in her youth in her father’s house.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Exact vengeance for the sons of Israel from the Midianites. Finally you shall be gathered to your people.
And Moses spoke to the people, saying: Equip men from among you to draw up for battle before the Lord against Midian, to repay Midian with vengeance from the Lord.
Send a thousand from each tribe, from all the tribes of Israel, to draw up for battle.
And they counted out a thousand from each tribe from the thousands of Israel: twelve thousand equipped for battle.
And Moses sent them, a thousand from each tribe, with their force and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, with the sacred vessels and the signalling trumpets in their hands.
And they drew up for battle against Midian, as the Lord had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
And they killed the kings of Midian together with their slain: Evi, Zur, Rekem, Hur, and Robok, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword together with their slain.
And they took the women of Midian and their dependents as spoil, and plundered their livestock, all their possessions, and their resources.
And they burned all their towns in their settlements and their farmsteads with fire.
And they took all the plunder and all their spoils, from people to livestock,
and brought the captives, the spoils, and the plunder unto Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the sons of Israel, at the camp at Araboth Moab, which is on the Jordan opposite Jericho.
And Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the rulers of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp.
And Moses was angry with the overseers of the force, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds who were returning from the battle formation,
and Moses said to them: Why have you taken every female alive?
For these women, according to Balaam’s word, caused the sons of Israel to turn away and disregard the Lord’s word because of Peor, and the plague came upon the Lord’s congregation.
And now kill every male among all the dependents, and kill every woman who has known a male’s bed.
Take alive all the female dependents who have not known a male’s bed.
And you shall camp outside the camp for seven days. Everyone who killed someone or touches someone slain shall be purified on the third day and the seventh day, both you and your captives.
And you shall thoroughly purify every covering, every leather article, every object made from goats’ hair, and every wooden article.
And Eleazar the priest said to the men of the force who were returning from the battle formation, This is the ordinance of the law that the Lord prescribed unto Moses:
Only the gold, and the silver, and the bronze, and the iron, and the lead, and the tin,
everything that passes through fire shall also be cleansed, but it shall be purified with the water of purification. Everything that does not pass through fire shall pass through water.
And you shall wash your clothes on the seventh day and be cleansed; afterward you shall enter the camp.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Take a total of the spoils of captivity, from people to livestock, you, Eleazar the priest, and the rulers of the congregation’s ancestral houses.
And you shall divide the spoils between the warriors who go forth into battle and the whole congregation.

And you shall set apart a levy unto the Lord from the warriors who went forth into battle: one living being out of five hundred, from the men, and from the livestock, and from the cattle, and from the sheep, and from the goats.
And you shall take it from their half; and you shall give unto Eleazar the priest the firstfruits of the Lord.

And from the half belonging to the sons of Israel you shall take one out of fifty, from the men, and from the cattle, and from the sheep, and from the donkeys, and from all the livestock; and you shall give them unto the Levites who keep the charges in the Tent of the Lord.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the Lord had prescribed unto Moses.
And the surplus of the plunder that the warriors had taken was six hundred seventy-five thousand sheep,
And seventy-two thousand cattle,
And sixty-one thousand donkeys,
and thirty-two thousand human beings in all, from the women who had not known a man’s bed.
And the half-share belonging to those who went out to war numbered three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,
and the levy for the Lord from the sheep was six hundred seventy-five.
And the cattle numbered thirty-six thousand, and the levy for the Lord was seventy-two.
And the donkeys numbered thirty thousand five hundred, and the levy for the Lord was sixty-one.
And the human beings numbered sixteen thousand, and their levy for the Lord was thirty-two persons.
And Moses gave the levy for the Lord, the portion set apart unto God, to Eleazar the priest, as the Lord had prescribed unto Moses.
From the half belonging to the sons of Israel, which Moses had separated from the warriors—
And the congregation’s half was three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,
And thirty-six thousand cattle,
thirty thousand five hundred donkeys,
and sixteen thousand human beings—

and Moses took from the half belonging to the sons of Israel one out of fifty, from the men and from the livestock, and gave them unto the Levites who kept the charges of the Tent of the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And all those appointed over the army’s units of a thousand, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, approached Moses.
And they said unto Moses: Your servants have counted the warriors in our company, and not even one of them is missing.
And we have brought the gift unto the Lord, each man whatever gold article he found—armlets, bracelets, rings, wrist ornaments, and hair ornaments—to make atonement for us before the Lord.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, every article worked by hand.
And all the gold, the portion set apart that they set aside for the Lord from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, was sixteen thousand seven hundred fifty shekels.
And the warriors had taken plunder, each for himself.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and brought it into the Tent of Testimony as a memorial for the sons of Israel before the Lord.
And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad had a multitude of livestock, a very great multitude; and they saw the country of Jazer and the country of Gilead, and the place was a place for livestock.
And the sons of Reuben and sons of Gad approached and said unto Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the rulers of the congregation:
Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sibmah, Nebo, and Beon—
the land that the Lord handed over before the sons of Israel—is land that nourishes livestock, and your servants have livestock.
And they said: If we have found favour before you, let this land be given to your servants as a possession. Do not make us cross the Jordan.
And Moses said to the sons of Gad and sons of Reuben: Your brothers are going to war, and will you sit here?
And why do you turn aside the minds of the sons of Israel so that they do not cross into the land that the Lord is giving them?
Did not your fathers do this when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to examine the land?
And they went up to the Ravine of the Cluster and examined the land, but turned away the hearts of the sons of Israel so that they would not enter the land that the Lord had given them.
And the Lord became fiercely angry on that day and swore, saying:
Surely these men who came up from Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, who know evil and good, shall not see the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, for they did not follow after Me,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh, the one set apart, and Joshua son of Nun, because he followed after the Lord.
And the Lord became fiercely angry with Israel and whirled them about in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole generation that did evil before the Lord had been consumed.
Behold, you have risen in your fathers’ place, a band of sinful men, to add still more to the fury of the Lord’s anger against Israel.
Because you will turn away from Him, He will again leave them in the wilderness, and you will act lawlessly against this whole congregation.
And they approached him and said: Let us build sheepfolds here for our livestock and towns for our dependents.

And we will equip ourselves as an advance guard ahead of the sons of Israel until we have brought them to their own place. Our dependents will live in walled towns because of the inhabitants of the land.
We will certainly not return to our homes until the sons of Israel have each been allotted his inheritance.
And we shall not inherit further among them across the Jordan and beyond, because we have received our allotments on the eastern side of the Jordan.
And Moses said to them: If you act according to this word, if you equip yourselves before the Lord for war,
and every armed man among you crosses the Jordan before the Lord until His enemy is wiped out from before Him,

and the land is brought under dominion before the Lord, then afterward you shall return. You shall be guiltless before the Lord and toward Israel, and this land shall be your possession before the Lord.
But if you do not do so, you shall sin before the Lord, and you shall recognize your sin when evils overtake you.
And you shall build for yourselves towns for your dependents and folds for your livestock; and you shall do that which comes out of your mouth.
And the sons of Reuben and sons of Gad said unto Moses: Your servants will do as our lord commands.
Our dependents, our wives, and all our livestock will remain in the towns of Gilead.
But your servants will cross over, all armed and drawn up in formation before the Lord for war, as the lord says.
And Moses appointed over them Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the rulers of the ancestral houses of the tribes of Israel.

And Moses said to them: If the sons of Reuben and sons of Gad cross the Jordan with you, everyone equipped for war before the Lord, and you gain dominion over the land before you, you shall give them the land of Gilead as a possession.

But if they do not cross over equipped with you for war before the Lord, you shall bring their dependents, their wives, and their livestock across ahead of you into the land of Canaan, and they shall receive an inheritance among you in the land of Canaan.
And the sons of Reuben and sons of Gad answered: Everything our lord says unto his servants, we will do.
We will cross over equipped before the Lord into the land of Canaan, and you shall give us our possession on this side of the Jordan.

And Moses gave to the sons of Gad, the sons of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, of the sons of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: the land and its towns with its boundaries, the towns of the surrounding land.
And the sons of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, and Aroer,
And Shophar and Jazer, and raised them up,
And Nimrah and Beth-haran, fortified towns and sheepfolds.
And the sons of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kiriathaim,
and Baal-meon, surrounded with defenses, and Sibmah. They named the towns they built according to their names.
And a son of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead and took it, and destroyed the Amorite who lived there.
And Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
And Jair of Manasseh went and took their settlements, and named them Settlements of Jair.
And Nabau went and took Kenath and its villages, and named them Naboth after his own name.
And these are the stations of the sons of Israel when they came out of the land of Egypt with their force under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
And Moses recorded their departures and their stations through the Lord’s word. These are the stations of their journey.
They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Passover, the sons of Israel went out with a high hand before all the Egyptians,
and the Egyptians were burying all their dead whom the Lord had struck down, every firstborn in the land of Egypt. The Lord also exacted vengeance upon their gods.
And the sons of Israel set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
And they set out from Succoth and camped at Bouthan, which is a part of the wilderness.
And they set out from Bouthan and camped at the mouth of Eiroth, which is opposite Baal-zephon, and camped opposite Migdol.
And they set out from opposite Eiroth and crossed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness. They themselves travelled three days through the wilderness and camped at Bitternesses.
And they set out from Bitternesses and came to Elim. At Elim were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there beside the water.
And they set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
And they set out from the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
And they set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Raphaka.
And they set out from Raphaka and camped at Alush.
And they set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, and there was no water there for the people to drink.
And they set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
And they set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Graves of Craving.
And they set out from Graves of Craving and camped at Hazeroth.
And they set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
And they set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
And they set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Lemonah.
And they set out from Lemonah and camped at Dessah.
And they set out from Dessah and camped at Makellath.
And they set out from Makellath and camped at Shaphar.
And they set out from Shaphar and camped at Haradah.
And they set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
And they set out from Makheloth and camped at Kataath.
And they set out from Kataath and camped at Tarath.
And they set out from Tarath and camped at Mithkah.
And they set out from Mithkah and camped at Zalmonah.
And they set out from Zalmonah and camped at Moseroth.
And they set out from Moseroth and camped at Banaia.
And they set out from Banaia and camped at Mount Gadgad.
And they set out from Mount Gadgad and camped at Jotbathah.
And they set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
And they set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
And they set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Sin. They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped in the wilderness of Paran, that is, Kadesh.
And they set out from Kadesh and camped at Hor the mountain, near the land of Edom.

And Aaron the priest went up by the Lord’s command and died there in the fortieth year of the departure of the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month.
And Aaron was one hundred twenty-three years old when he died on Hor the mountain.
And the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the land of Canaan, heard when the sons of Israel were entering.
And they set out from Hor the mountain and camped at Zalmonah.
And they set out from Zalmonah and camped at Phino.
And they set out from Phino and camped at Oboth.
And they set out from Oboth and camped at Gai on the other side, at the borders of Moab.
And they set out from Gai and camped at Dibon-Gad.
And they set out from Dibon-Gad and camped at Gelmon-diblathaim.
And they set out from Gelmon-diblathaim and camped at the mountains of Abarim, opposite Nebo.
And they set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped on the western side of Moab, by the Jordan opposite Jericho.
And they camped beside the Jordan from Aisimoth to Belshittim, on the western side of Moab.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses on the western side of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: You are crossing the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
and you shall destroy all who inhabit the land before you, remove their lookout places, destroy all their cast idols, and remove all their pillars.
And you shall destroy all who inhabit the land and settle in it, for I have given you their land as an allotment.

And you shall inherit their land by lot according to your tribes. Increase the possession of the larger groups and decrease that of the smaller groups. Wherever his name comes out shall be his. You shall inherit according to the tribes of your ancestral houses.

But if you do not destroy the inhabitants of the land from before you, those whom you leave will become splinters in your eyes and missiles in your sides, and they will act as enemies in the land where you shall settle.
And then I will do to you what I had determined to do to them.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Command the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: You are entering the land of Canaan; this shall be your inheritance, the land of Canaan with its boundaries.
And your southwestern side shall run from the wilderness of Sin to the territory adjoining Edom. Your southwestern boundary shall begin from the part of the Salt Sea toward the east.

And the boundary shall turn around you from the southwest toward the Ascent of Akrabin and pass through Senna. Its endpoint shall be southwest of Kadesh-barnea; it shall extend to the settlement of Arad and pass through Azmon.
And the boundary shall turn from Azmon to the Wadi of Egypt, and its endpoint shall be the sea.
And for your sea boundary, the Great Sea shall mark the limit. This shall be your sea boundary.
And this shall be your boundary toward the north: from the Great Sea you shall measure out for yourselves beside the mountain, the mountain;
and from the mountain, the mountain, you shall measure out for them toward the entrance into Hamath; and its endpoint shall be the boundaries of Sarada.
And the boundary shall extend to Dephrona, and its endpoint shall be Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern boundary.
And you shall measure out for yourselves the eastern boundary from Hazar-enan unto Shepham.
And the boundary shall descend from Shepham to Arbela, from the east toward the springs. The boundary shall descend to Bela, along the eastern ridge of the Sea of Chennara.
And the boundary shall descend to the Jordan, and its endpoint shall be the Salt Sea. This shall be your land and its surrounding boundaries.
And Moses commanded the sons of Israel, saying: This is the land that you shall inherit by lot, as the Lord prescribed unto Moses to give to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
For the tribe of the sons of Reuben and the tribe of the sons of Gad according to their ancestral houses, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, have received their allotments.
The two tribes and the half-tribe have received their allotments across the Jordan opposite Jericho, from the south toward the east.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
These are the names of the men who shall obtain the land as an inheritance for you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
And you shall take one ruler from each tribe to allot the land unto you.
And these are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Simeon, Salamiel son of Ammihud;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Eldad son of Chislon;
from the tribe of Dan, the ruler Bakchir son of Egli;
from the descendants of Joseph, from the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, the ruler Hanniel son of Ouphi;
from the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, the ruler Kemuel son of Sabatha;
from the tribe of Zebulun, the ruler Elizaphan son of Parnach;
from the tribe of the sons of Issachar, the ruler Paltiel son of Oza;
from the tribe of the sons of Asher, the ruler Achior son of Shelomi;
from the tribe of Naphtali, the ruler Pedahel son of Benammihud.
These are the men whom the Lord commanded to distribute portions to the sons of Israel in the land of Canaan.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses on the western side of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying:
Instruct the sons of Israel to give the Levites towns to live in from their allotted possessions. They shall also give the Levites the outlying lands around the towns.
And the towns shall be theirs to live in, and their designated lands shall be for their livestock and all their four-footed animals.
And the lands adjoining the towns that you shall give the Levites shall extend two thousand cubits outward from the town wall all around.

And you shall measure outside the town two thousand cubits on the eastern side, and two thousand cubits on the southwestern side, and two thousand cubits on the seaward side, and two thousand cubits on the northern side; and the town shall be in the midst thereof for you, together with the adjoining lands of the towns.
And you shall give the Levites the six cities of refuge that you shall provide for the person who has killed someone to flee to, and in addition to these, forty-two towns.
All the towns you shall give the Levites shall be forty-eight towns, together with their outlying lands.

And for the towns that you shall give from the possession of the sons of Israel, take many from those with much and fewer from those with less. Each shall give towns to the Levites according to the inheritance he receives.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: You are crossing the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
and you shall set apart towns for yourselves. They shall be refuges for the killer to flee there, anyone who has struck a person unintentionally.
And the towns shall be refuges for you from the kinsman who avenges blood, so that the killer shall in no wise die before standing before the congregation for judgment.
And the towns you shall provide, the six towns, shall be refuges for you.
You shall provide three towns across the Jordan, and you shall provide three towns in the land of Canaan.

There shall be a refuge for the sons of Israel; for the sojourner and the resident stranger among you, these towns shall also be refuges, so that anyone who strikes a person unintentionally may flee there.
But if he strikes someone with an iron object and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.
If he strikes someone with a stone from his hand capable of causing death and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.
If he strikes someone with a wooden object from his hand capable of causing death and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.
The kinsman who avenges blood shall himself kill the murderer. When he encounters him, he shall kill him.
If he pushes someone out of enmity and throws an object at him from ambush and that person dies,

or strikes him with his hand out of wrath and he dies, let the one who struck him surely be put to death; he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death. The kinsman who avenges blood shall kill the murderer when he encounters him.
But if he suddenly pushes someone without enmity, or throws any object at him without ambush,
or, without his knowing, a stone capable of causing death falls upon him and he dies, though he was not his enemy and was not seeking to harm him,
And then the congregation shall judge between the one who struck him and the kinsman who avenges blood according to these judgments.

And the congregation shall rescue the killer from the kinsman who avenges blood and restore him to the city of refuge to which he fled. He shall live there until the high priest dies, whom they anointed with the holy oil.
But if the killer goes outside the boundaries of the city to which he fled,
and the kinsman who avenges blood finds him outside the boundaries of his city of refuge and kills the killer, the avenger is not liable.
For he must live in the city of refuge until the high priest dies. After the death of the high priest, the killer may return to the land of his possession.
And these shall be an ordinance of judgment for you throughout your generations in all your settlements.
In every case of a person being struck down, you shall put the killer to death through witnesses. A single witness shall not testify against a person so as to cause his death.
And you shall not accept a ransom for a life from the killer who is guilty and liable to be killed; he shall surely be put to death.
You shall not accept a ransom concerning flight to a city of refuge, allowing him to live in the land again before the high priest dies.

And you shall in no wise stain with murder the land wherein you dwell; for this blood stains the land with murder, and atonement shall not be made for the land for the blood shed upon it, except by the blood of him who shed it.
And you shall not defile the land in which you dwell, in which I will dwell among you, for I am the Lord, dwelling among the sons of Israel.

And the rulers of the tribe of the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the tribe of Joseph’s descendants, approached and spoke before Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the rulers of the ancestral houses of the sons of Israel.

And they said: The Lord commanded our lord to distribute the inherited land by lot to the sons of Israel, and the Lord instructed the lord to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

And if they become wives in one of the Israelite tribes, their allotment will be taken from our fathers’ possession and added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry. It will be taken from our inherited allotment.

If the release comes for the sons of Israel, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry, and their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our ancestral tribe.
And Moses commanded the sons of Israel by the Lord’s instruction, saying: Thus speaks the tribe of Joseph’s descendants.
This is the word that the Lord prescribed concerning Zelophehad’s daughters: Let them marry whom they please, but they shall marry from their father’s clan.
And no inheritance among the sons of Israel shall pass from tribe to tribe, for each Israelite shall hold fast to the inheritance of his ancestral tribe.

And every daughter who succeeds as next of kin to an inheritance among the Israelite tribes shall marry someone from her father’s clan, so that each Israelite may succeed as next of kin to his paternal inheritance.
And no allotment shall pass from one tribe to another; rather, the sons of Israel shall each hold fast to their own inheritance.
Zelophehad’s daughters did as the Lord had prescribed unto Moses.
And Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, Noah, and Mahlah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married their cousins.
They married within the clan of Manasseh, of Joseph’s descendants, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of their father’s clan.
These are the commandments, ordinances, and judgments that the Lord commanded through Moses on the western side of Moab, by the Jordan opposite Jericho.
